main_text.l: IMPROBI socios malorum quærunt. Epid. I.I.v.70.
HERCULI pars decima de prædâ bonorum dabatur. Bacch. 4.4.v.15.
IN monumentum & memoriam rerum gestarum, solebant erigere statuas aureas. Curc. 3.I.v, 70. Ubi ridiculè exagitatur miles Thrasonicus.

PANATHENAICIS magnis, quorum feriæ quinquennales erant, Peplus, seu Peplum Athenis Minervæ consecrabatur, cui intexta erat Titanomachia, & victoria Palladis de Encelado. Merc. Prol. v.67. Servius ad illud Virgil. lib.1. Æneid. Interea ad templum, non aquæ Palladis ibant (crinibus Iliades passis, peplumq; ferebant.
Ubi Turneb. libr. 14. cap. 15. Peplum Trojanæ mulieres ferunt, ut câ vestè Minervæ simulacrum induant, & Deam propitiam habeant.

page.notes: Catchword "Cc" at foot; the line "Cc habeant." is a signature/catchword at the foot and was kept with its text. Greek word in the Diodorus line is printed in Greek letters and transcribed as near as legible; the Latin word "Titanomachia" and some italic lines are approximate.
